blocks.source: Vol IV, Spatial Memory, § Fallacies and Pitfalls
blocks.md: Evaluating a spatial memory architecture requires auditing how separate state beliefs interact across time, coordinate frames, and physical occupancy. In physical AI, planning failures frequently occur when systems treat software records as static facts rather than time-decaying physical hypotheses. Two records can each be internally valid and fresh according to local timestamps, yet combining them without temporal reconciliation yields an inconsistent or hazardous model of the workspace. Before authorizing mechanical motion, a real-time controller must reconcile disparate sensor epochs, velocity bounds, and physical occlusion boundaries.

questions.q: The section **Fallacies and Pitfalls** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A filter's reported covariance is a hypothesis tested offline by NEES against ground truth and online by NIS on innovations, and an above-band mean flags the safety-critical overconfident filter.

When distinct state histories give identical measurements no estimator can separate them, and innovations stay near zero while the true state drifts, so observability must be designed in by excitation or added sensing.
Every spatial claim carries evidence, estimate, and publication epochs, and only a physical measurement advances the evidence epoch, so prediction and republishing must preserve it.
A metric loop at camera rate keeps geometry current while foundation backbones update semantics on keyframes, and semantics never certify clearance.
